title: CPM worker's murder, LDF govt's probe: But only 3 convictions in Dhanaraj murder as court flags mechanical investigation
content: Kannur: Slain CPM worker C V Dhanaraj (38) was at the centre of political debate in Kannur in the run-up to the Assembly election after whistleblower V Kunhikrishnan accused CPM leaders of misappropriating money collected for his family. The allegations, which implicated Payyannur MLA and CPM leader T I Madhusoodanan, fuelled dissent within the party and contributed to the CPM's fall in Payyannur, one of its strongest bastions, and the eventual victory of Kunhikrishnan, whom party workers believed and embraced. The verdict in the decade-old murder case has now brought Dhanaraj's killing back to haunt the CPM, this time over the failure of the prosecution to secure convictions against most of those it accused. A prosecution that alleged a politically motivated conspiracy involving 20 people ended with only three convictions. Sixteen of the 19 accused who faced trial were acquitted, and the court made an unusually sharp observation about the quality of the police investigation. The Taliparamba Additional Sessions Court found T P Biju, M Vipin and his brother M Vaishakh guilty of murdering Dhanaraj at his home in Ramanthali on July 11, 2016. But it acquitted them of the charges relating to abetment, conspiracy and unlawful assembly, among others. The other 16 accused were acquitted of all charges, with the court giving them the benefit of doubt. The sentence will be pronounced on Wednesday. Despite the seriousness of a sensational murder case, the investigating team mechanically conducted the probe, resulting in lapses, the court observed. It also said effective investigation was a constitutional requirement. The court found the evidence insufficient to establish the involvement of the other accused. The verdict is being seen as a loss of face for the CPM, as the investigation and prosecution unfolded under the LDF government during its decade in power, when the party controlled the Home Department. The defence counsel, Adv P Padmarajan, said even the three convictions hinged on a flawed identification parade. "We feel it was a moral judgment. Nothing else linked the accused to the crime. We are sure we will get an acquittal in the higher court," he told Onmanorama. Two killings on a night The murder took place on a night that saw another politically charged killing in Payyannur. Hours after Dhanaraj was hacked to death in front of his mother, C V Madhavi, and wife, N V Sajina, RSS worker C K Ramachandran, an autorickshaw driver, was attacked inside his house at Annoor in Payyannur and killed. The two murders were followed by further violence in the region. In May 2017, C Biju alias Choorakkad Biju, the 12th accused in the Dhanaraj case, was also killed in an alleged retaliatory attack. The investigation into Dhanaraj's murder began with a claim that a BJP-RSS gang had followed him on motorcycles and attacked him as he reached home. His mother Madhavi and wife Sajina were the key eyewitnesses. The prosecution also relied on the testimony of neighbour Prajeesh, the first witness and complainant, and crucially a CPM branch secretary. But the court found Prajeesh's testimony unreliable because of his political connection. Defence counsel Adv Premarajan said the police had built the initial case around a list of suspects supplied by a witness who had not seen the murder. The FIR itself was manipulated to frame several people affiliated to the RSS and the BJP, Premarajan said. Of the three men eventually convicted, only Vipin was named in the FIR. His younger brother Vaishakh and TP Biju were not. Instead, the FIR named another person, Pandaravalappil Biju. Sangh Parivar functionaries who lived five to 10 kilometres from the crime scene, people working elsewhere and a Yuva Morcha mandalam president were also named, he said. Some of those names were later dropped by the police themselves. As I said, the intention was to implicate innocent people. We continue to maintain that accused Nos. 1 to 3 were framed, he said...
